# How One Notification Setting Changed Our Dinner Table

I made a simple change last week-turning off notifications on my phone during dinner-and it transformed everything.

Our dinners had become quiet. I'd be scrolling through work emails while my daughter babbled about her day, half-listening. The blue glow would reflect in her eyes as she showed me drawings, waiting for my attention that was always split between her and whatever ping just came through.

Then I tried something obvious but hard: leaving my phone in another room.

The first night felt awkward. My hand kept reaching for nothing. But then something shifted. My daughter got louder, funnier. She started telling me stories-not just "Mommy look!" but actual narratives about her stuffed animals' adventures. Her words were getting more complex. At two, she's building sentences now, connecting ideas.

I'd been too busy to notice.

Research from the University of California shows that even having a phone present during family meals-even if you're not actively using it-influences how much kids engage with their parents. They pull back. We all do.

Now dinner feels different. Messier, honestly. She throws pasta. I have to actually listen to her questions about why clouds are white (I don't know, sweetie). But we're talking again. Really talking.

The best part? It's contagious. My partner joined in. Now neither of us brings devices to the table.

Turns out the most important technology is the one that's been around for thousands of years: eye contact over food.

What's one small screen boundary you could try this week?
